questions.q: What are the three phases of a Gradle build, in order?
o: Initialization, configuration, execution
Configuration, initialization, execution
Compilation, testing, packaging
Resolution, execution, publication
questions.w: Initialization picks the projects, configuration builds the task graph without running tasks, and execution runs the requested tasks.

questions.q: A task shows UP-TO-DATE in the output. What does that mean?
o: Its inputs and outputs match the last run, so Gradle skipped the work
It was loaded from a remote cache on a shared server
It could not run because it has no source files
It finished successfully and has just been executed
questions.w: Gradle compares fingerprints of inputs and outputs. FROM-CACHE means restored from the cache, and NO-SOURCE means there was nothing to process.

questions.q: Which dependency configuration should you use for a library whose types appear in your module's public method signatures?
o: api
implementation
runtimeOnly
compileOnly
questions.w: api exposes the dependency to modules that compile against yours. With implementation, consumers cannot see its types and fail to compile.

questions.q: What is the main benefit of using implementation instead of api?
o: A change in the library does not force dependent modules to recompile
The library is excluded from the runtime classpath of the application
The library is downloaded only when a test needs it
The dependency version is chosen by the highest version rule
questions.w: implementation keeps the dependency off consumers' compile classpath, so fewer modules are recompiled, and the classpath stays small.

questions.q: Two libraries need different versions of Jackson. Which does Gradle choose by default?
o: The highest version requested anywhere in the graph
The version nearest to the root project
The version declared first in the build file
None, and the build fails until you choose one
questions.w: Gradle picks the highest version, unlike Maven's nearest definition. dependencyInsight shows why a version was selected.

questions.q: Why should a build script avoid doing real work directly at the top level?
o: Top-level code runs in the configuration phase on every build
Top-level code is ignored unless a task is run explicitly
Top-level code runs only after all tasks have finished
Top-level code cannot read files from the project directory
questions.w: Configuration runs on every invocation, so slow code there delays all builds and breaks the configuration cache. Do work in task actions.

questions.q: How does the build cache differ from the up-to-date check?
o: It reuses outputs from any earlier run, including other machines or CI
It only works while the Gradle daemon is running in memory
It compares the new build with the previous run of the same task only
It stores downloaded dependency jars outside the project
questions.w: The build cache is keyed by an input hash and can be shared remotely. The up-to-date check only looks at the last run in the same workspace.

questions.q: How should shared build logic be organised in a large multi-project build?
o: In convention plugins that each project applies
In allprojects blocks copied into every build file
In a single build file that lists every task by hand
In environment variables read by each project
questions.w: Convention plugins in build-logic or buildSrc keep configuration in one place, are easier to cache and read than allprojects and subprojects blocks.
